criteria: Every selected image was checked at full available resolution for exact species identity or exact accepted synonym, visible diagnostic traits, range-consistent provenance, composition, sharpness, and a reusable CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, or public-domain license. Near relatives, maps, skeletons, isolated body parts, obscured subjects, and low-resolution alternatives were rejected. Where no adequately licensed live image existed, an exact public-domain scientific plate was preferred over a misleading or poor-quality photograph.

approvals.visual_result: Exact historical color plate with the full animal, raised mane, warning stripe, short legs and bushy tail clearly visible. Open-license searches found no live image that met both resolution and presentation standards; the available live file was only 350 by 291 pixels, and the larger photographs were museum mounts.

approvals.visual_result: Sharp frontal underwater view from Cabo Douglas in the Galapagos; the bright red lips, flattened triangular head, rostral lure and limb-like pectoral fins are all visible.

approvals.attribution: (c) Piotr Lukasik, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: Full living animal photographed in eastern Madagascar; leaf-vein body pattern, angular head, fringed outline and ragged leaf-shaped tail are sharply visible in natural litter.

approvals.attribution: (c) Donna Belder, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: Clear full dorsal view from the Kimberley; the exceptionally robust body, conspicuous parotoid glands, white dorsal flecks and yellow limbs distinguish this species. Pelodryas splendida is the current iNaturalist name for the same accepted species concept.

approvals.attribution: (c) Bill Levine, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: Sharp full adult on a broken snag in Ecuador, within the post-split South American range; huge mouth, yellow eye and cryptic bark-like plumage are visible.

approvals.attribution: (c) Peter Archdale, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: Sharp Kenyan habitat photograph showing a full adult standing upright to browse, with a calf below; elongated neck, narrow head and diagnostic bipedal feeding posture are visible.

approvals.attribution: (c) Harshjeet Singh Bal, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: Sharp full exact-taxon individual on a tree in Kerala; long tail, angular head, bark camouflage and folded rib-supported patagium are visible. More open-winged candidates were too distant or blurred.

approvals.attribution: (c) Tia Offner, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: High-resolution stranded Atlantic female from Texas with mantle, eye, arms and violet-white web surfaces clearly visible. It is handled because no reusable in-water photograph of this exact Atlantic species passed review; attractive Indo-Pacific blanket-octopus images were rejected as likely Tremoctopus gracilis.

approvals.attribution: (c) Emanuel Kern, some rights reserved (CC BY)
approvals.visual_result: Exceptionally sharp full lateral living adult on vegetation in French Guiana; the globular branched pronotum, long posterior spine, wing venation and banded body are unobscured.
High-resolution full animal on wet rock; the long flexible proboscis, small eyes, enlarged webbed hind foot, flattened tail and water-adapted pelage are clearly visible.
